The present invention is directed to a method, apparatus, and computer-readable medium for utilizing a shared computer system. The method includes receiving, via at least one interface, an access request associated with a potential user seeking access to a secure data processing center. outputs.L2: The invention relates to a method, device, and computer-readable storage medium for making use of a shared computing system. The method involves receiving, through one or more interfaces, a request from a prospective user seeking entry to a secure data processing center. The request may then be handled or evaluated by one or more processors. Based on the processed request, the system may assign the prospective user a category corresponding to one or more possible or existing access privileges for the secure data processing center. The assigned category may identify the prospective user as at least one of the following: a non-user, an eligible user, a restricted user, or an approved user of the secure data processing center. As part of this classification process, the method includes determining whether the prospective user is connected with an organization that is a financial institution, a healthcare organization, a national security organization, a law enforcement organization, an educational organization, or any combination of these.
outputs.L3:
The invention describes a method, an apparatus, and a computer-readable medium for managing access to a shared secure computer system, such as a secure data processing center. The invention is directed to controlling and evaluating requests for access to secure computing resources, data, applications, or services, particularly where access may be shared among multiple users or organizations and where different users may be entitled to different levels of access.

In one implementation, the method includes receiving an access request from a potential user through at least one interface. The interface may include, for example, a web portal, application programming interface, client application, authentication terminal, network gateway, mobile device interface, or any other suitable mechanism through which a user may request access to the secure computer system. The access request may include identifying information, authentication credentials, affiliation information, requested permissions, purpose of access, device information, location information, or other data relevant to determining whether and how the potential user should be permitted to access the system.

At least one processor processes the access request to evaluate the potential user. This processing may include verifying identity, validating credentials, checking authorization records, comparing the request against stored access policies, reviewing organizational affiliation, determining whether the user has previously been granted access, and assessing whether the requested access is consistent with applicable security rules. The processor may access one or more databases, directories, policy engines, credential systems, or external verification services to perform the evaluation.

Based on the evaluation, the system determines a classification for the potential user. The classification may be based on the potential user’s actual access rights, potential access rights, organizational relationship, role, authorization status, or eligibility to access the secure data processing center. The classification is used to determine whether access should be denied, granted, restricted, monitored, or subjected to further approval.

For example, the potential user may be classified as a non-user, an eligible user, a limited user, or an authorized user. A non-user may be an individual or entity that has no current relationship to the secure system and no recognized right or eligibility to access it. An eligible user may be a person or entity that satisfies certain preliminary requirements for access but has not yet been granted full authorization. A limited user may be permitted to access only certain resources, functions, data sets, or services within the secure system, possibly subject to time, role, purpose, or transaction-based restrictions. An authorized user may be a user who has been fully approved to access the secure computer system in accordance with applicable policies and credentials.

The classification may also depend on the potential user’s association with one or more entities or organizations. Such entities may include, without limitation, financial institutions, health care organizations, national security agencies, law enforcement organizations, educational institutions, governmental bodies, contractors, service providers, or other trusted or regulated organizations. For instance, a user associated with a financial institution may be evaluated according to policies governing financial data access, while a user associated with a health care organization may be evaluated under policies applicable to protected health information. Similarly, users associated with national security or law enforcement organizations may be classified according to heightened security, clearance, or mission-based requirements.

The apparatus for carrying out the method may include one or more interfaces for receiving access requests, at least one processor for evaluating the requests, and one or more memory devices storing instructions, user records, access policies, classification rules, and authorization data. When executed by the processor, the stored instructions cause the apparatus to receive the access request, process information associated with the potential user, determine the appropriate classification, and manage access to the shared secure computer system based on that classification.

The computer-readable medium may store instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the processors to perform the access management operations described above. In this manner, the invention provides a structured and automated approach for evaluating potential users and controlling access to secure computing resources according to user classification, organizational affiliation, and applicable access rights.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to systems and techniques for controlling access to a secure shared data processing center. More particularly, the invention provides a method, apparatus, and computer-readable medium configured to receive, evaluate, and manage requests for access to computing resources, data, applications, or services maintained within a secure shared environment. The secure shared data processing center may be used by multiple organizations or entities and may contain sensitive, confidential, regulated, or mission-critical information. Accordingly, the invention enables access to be granted, limited, denied, or modified based on predetermined access rights, user status, organizational affiliation, and applicable security rules.

In one embodiment, an access management system includes one or more communication interfaces configured to receive access requests from potential users. The access requests may be submitted through a network, portal, application programming interface, terminal, workstation, mobile device, or other electronic interface. Each request may include information identifying the requesting party, the entity with which the requesting party is associated, the type of access requested, the resources sought, credentials, authentication data, or other relevant access-control information.

The system further includes one or more processors configured to process the received access requests. Processing may include authenticating the identity of the requester, determining whether the requester is associated with an approved or recognized entity, comparing the request against stored access policies, and determining the requester’s access classification. The processors may communicate with databases, directories, identity-management systems, credential repositories, audit logs, or external verification services in order to evaluate the access request.

The invention classifies potential users into one or more access categories. A potential user may be classified as a non-user when the person or system has no recognized access rights to the secure shared data processing center. A potential user may be classified as an eligible user when the user is associated with an approved entity or otherwise satisfies threshold eligibility requirements but has not yet been granted full access. A potential user may be classified as a limited user when the user is permitted to access only certain resources, functions, datasets, or services within the secure shared data processing center. A potential user may be classified as an authorized user when the user has been approved for access in accordance with applicable rules and is permitted to use one or more designated resources of the center.

The entities associated with potential users may include, without limitation, financial institutions, healthcare organizations, national security agencies, law enforcement organizations, educational institutions, governmental bodies, research organizations, or other entities that require controlled access to shared data processing resources. Because such entities may operate under different legal, regulatory, contractual, or operational requirements, the system may apply different access rules depending on the user’s affiliation, role, clearance level, credential status, geographic location, or purpose for requesting access.

In operation, the system receives an access request from a potential user and determines whether the potential user is known to the system. If the user is not known or lacks any applicable right to access the secure shared data processing center, the system may classify the requester as a non-user and deny access. If the requester is associated with a recognized entity but has not completed all requirements for access, the system may classify the requester as an eligible user and may initiate additional enrollment, verification, approval, or credentialing steps. If the requester is approved for only a subset of resources, the system may classify the requester as a limited user and provide access only to those resources for which authorization exists. If the requester has satisfied all applicable requirements, the system may classify the requester as an authorized user and permit access according to the user’s assigned permissions.

The access management system may also update user classifications over time. For example, an eligible user may become an authorized user after completing verification or receiving approval from an administrator. An authorized user may be downgraded to a limited user if permissions are reduced, if a credential expires, or if access is restricted due to a policy change. A limited user or authorized user may be reclassified as a non-user if the user is no longer associated with an approved entity, violates security requirements, or otherwise loses access rights. These classification changes may be recorded in audit logs and may be communicated to administrators or integrated security systems.

The invention may further include security features such as multi-factor authentication, role-based access control, attribute-based access control, encryption, session monitoring, policy enforcement, anomaly detection, and automated alerts. The system may maintain records of access requests, approvals, denials, classifications, changes in access status, and activities performed within the secure shared data processing center. Such records may support compliance, auditing, incident response, reporting, and administrative review.

The computer-readable medium of the invention may store instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the processors to perform the access management functions described above. These functions may include receiving access requests, identifying a requester, determining an association between the requester and an entity, evaluating access rights, classifying the requester as a non-user, eligible user, limited user, or authorized user, granting or denying access based on the classification, and updating access records. The computer-readable medium may be non-transitory and may include memory, storage devices, servers, cloud-based storage, or other suitable media.

By classifying users according to access rights and entity association, the invention provides a structured and secure approach for managing access to a shared data processing environment. The invention helps ensure that sensitive resources are made available only to appropriate users, while also allowing organizations from different sectors, such as finance, healthcare, national security, law enforcement, and education, to participate in a controlled shared computing infrastructure.
outputs.L5:
**The Power of “The”**

The word **“the”** may seem small, but it plays an important role in English. It is called a definite article, and it helps us talk about something specific. For example, when we say “a book,” we could mean any book. But when we say “the book,” we mean one particular book that the speaker and listener both understand.

“The” appears everywhere in everyday speech and writing. It helps make sentences clearer and more precise. We use it when talking about things that are unique, such as **the sun**, **the moon**, or **the sky**. We also use it when something has already been mentioned: “I saw a dog. The dog was friendly.”

Although it is only three letters long, “the” is one of the most common and useful words in the English language. It connects ideas, gives meaning, and helps people understand exactly what is being discussed. Sometimes the smallest words have the biggest impact.

counterfactuals.output: A method, system, and computer-readable medium are provided for controlling access to a secure shared data processing center. A request to access one or more computing resources of the shared data processing center is received from a user device and associated with user-identifying information and organization-identifying information. The user is classified according to one or more user categories, such as employee, contractor, administrator, partner, or guest, based at least in part on authentication data, credential attributes, assigned roles, and historical access information. An organization type associated with the user is determined and verified against permitted organization classifications, such as governmental, enterprise, healthcare, financial, educational, or approved third-party entities. Access to the shared data processing center is selectively granted, restricted, monitored, or denied based on a policy evaluation combining the user classification, the verified organization type, requested resource, security posture of the user device, and contextual access parameters. The system may generate audit records, apply dynamic access rules, require additional authentication, and modify permissions in real time in response to changes in user classification or organization type.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate legalistic patent language for a system that receives access requests, determines user eligibility levels, and identifies whether the requester is affiliated with finance, healthcare, national security, law enforcement, or education.
counterfactuals.output:
Below is sample legalistic patent-style language for the described system.

---

## Abstract

A computerized access-control system receives an access request from a requester, obtains or derives requester attributes, determines an eligibility level associated with the requester, and classifies the requester as affiliated with one or more regulated or sensitive sectors, including finance, healthcare, national security, law enforcement, or education. Based at least in part on the eligibility level and the sector affiliation, the system generates an access determination, access policy selection, audit record, or workflow routing instruction.

---

## Example Patent Specification Language

In some embodiments, a computer-implemented system is provided for evaluating access requests and determining access permissions based on requester eligibility and sector affiliation. The system may comprise one or more processors, memory storing computer-executable instructions, and one or more network interfaces configured to receive access requests from requester devices.

An access request may include, or may be associated with, requester-identifying information, authentication information, organizational information, credential information, role information, domain information, certificate information, metadata, device information, network-origin information, or other attributes usable to evaluate a requester. Upon receiving the access request, the system may query one or more internal or external data sources to obtain supplemental requester information, including directory records, identity-provider records, employment records, licensing records, agency records, institutional records, compliance records, or prior access-history records.

The system may determine an eligibility level for the requester. The eligibility level may represent a degree, tier, classification, authorization status, clearance status, role-based permission level, trust score, risk-adjusted access level, compliance qualification, or other access-related category. In certain embodiments, the eligibility level is determined by applying rules, policies, scoring logic, machine-learning models, credential verification logic, or combinations thereof to the requester attributes.

The system may further identify whether the requester is affiliated with one or more predetermined sectors. Such sectors may include finance, healthcare, national security, law enforcement, and education. Sector affiliation may be determined based on an employer identifier, organizational domain, professional credential, license, agency membership, institution identifier, network address, contract identifier, user profile attribute, self-attestation, third-party verification, or other evidence of affiliation.

In some embodiments, the system maps requester attributes to a sector-affiliation taxonomy. The taxonomy may include one or more finance affiliation categories, healthcare affiliation categories, national-security affiliation categories, law-enforcement affiliation categories, and education affiliation categories. The system may assign one or more confidence values to each identified affiliation and may resolve conflicts where a requester is associated with multiple sectors.

Based at least in part on the determined eligibility level and the identified sector affiliation, the system may generate an access decision. The access decision may include granting access, denying access, limiting access, requiring additional verification, escalating the request for review, selecting a data-handling policy, applying masking or redaction rules, limiting functionality, imposing logging requirements, or assigning a workflow for approval.

The system may generate and store an audit record comprising the access request, requester attributes, eligibility level, sector affiliation, policy rules applied, confidence values, and access determination. The audit record may be stored in a tamper-resistant log, compliance database, distributed ledger, or other auditable storage medium.

---

## Example Independent System Claim

1. A system comprising:  
   one or more processors; and  
   one or more non-transitory computer-readable storage media storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the system to:  
   receive, from a requester device, an access request associated with a requester;  
   obtain requester attribute data associated with the requester;  
   determine, based at least in part on the requester attribute data, an eligibility level of the requester;  
   identify, based at least in part on the requester attribute data, whether the requester is affiliated with at least one sector selected from a group consisting of finance, healthcare, national security, law enforcement, and education; and  
   generate an access-control output based at least in part on the eligibility level and the identified sector affiliation.

---

## Example Dependent Claims

2. The system of claim 1, wherein the requester attribute data comprises at least one of an organizational identifier, a user role, an identity-provider attribute, a digital certificate, a domain name, a professional credential, an employment record, or a network-origin attribute.

3. The system of claim 1, wherein determining the eligibility level comprises applying a policy rule set to the requester attribute data.

4. The system of claim 1, wherein determining the eligibility level comprises generating a numerical trust score and mapping the numerical trust score to one of a plurality of access tiers.

5. The system of claim 1, wherein identifying the sector affiliation comprises comparing an organizational domain associated with the requester to a stored mapping of domains to sector classifications.

6. The system of claim 1, wherein identifying the sector affiliation comprises querying an external data source to verify a credential associated with the requester.

7. The system of claim 1, wherein the access-control output comprises an access grant, an access denial, a request for additional authentication, a request for human review, or a restricted-access authorization.

8. The system of claim 1, wherein the access-control output comprises a data-handling policy selected based on the identified sector affiliation.

9. The system of claim 8, wherein the data-handling policy comprises at least one of a redaction policy, encryption policy, retention policy, logging policy, or disclosure-limitation policy.

10. The system of claim 1, wherein the instructions further cause the system to assign a confidence score to the identified sector affiliation.

11. The system of claim 10, wherein the instructions further cause the system to resolve a plurality of candidate sector affiliations based at least in part on respective confidence scores.

12. The system of claim 1, wherein the requester is determined to be affiliated with more than one of finance, healthcare, national security, law enforcement, or education.

13. The system of claim 1, wherein the eligibility level is selected from a plurality of predetermined eligibility tiers.

14. The system of claim 1, wherein the instructions further cause the system to generate an audit record comprising the access request, the eligibility level, the identified sector affiliation, and the access-control output.

15. The system of claim 14, wherein the audit record is stored in tamper-resistant storage.

16. The system of claim 1, wherein the requester attribute data is obtained from an identity provider using a federated authentication protocol.

17. The system of claim 1, wherein the requester attribute data is obtained from a directory service associated with an organization of the requester.

18. The system of claim 1, wherein the sector affiliation is identified using a sector-affiliation taxonomy stored in memory.

19. The system of claim 1, wherein the eligibility level is determined using both role-based access criteria and risk-based access criteria.

20. The system of claim 1, wherein the access request relates to access to at least one protected data resource, software function, network service, application programming interface, or controlled workflow.

---

## Example Method Claim

21. A computer-implemented method comprising:  
   receiving, by one or more processors, an access request associated with a requester;  
   obtaining requester attribute data associated with the requester;  
   determining, by the one or more processors and based at least in part on the requester attribute data, an eligibility level corresponding to the requester;  
   identifying, by the one or more processors and based at least in part on the requester attribute data, whether the requester is affiliated with one or more sectors comprising finance, healthcare, national security, law enforcement, or education; and  
   producing, by the one or more processors, an access-control output based at least in part on the eligibility level and the one or more identified sectors.

---

## Example Non-Transitory Computer-Readable Medium Claim

22. One or more non-transitory computer-readable media storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform operations comprising:  
   receiving an access request associated with a requester;  
   retrieving requester attribute data from at least one identity data source;  
   determining an eligibility level of the requester based on the requester attribute data;  
   classifying the requester as affiliated or not affiliated with each of a plurality of sectors comprising finance, healthcare, national security, law enforcement, and education; and  
   generating an access-control output based on the eligibility level and the classification.

---

## Additional Embodiment Language

In certain embodiments, the system may employ configurable policy logic that permits different access outcomes for different combinations of eligibility levels and sector affiliations. For example, a requester associated with a healthcare sector and having a first eligibility level may receive access to a first category of resources, while a requester associated with law enforcement and having the same eligibility level may receive access to a second category of resources. In further embodiments, a requester associated with national security may be subject to additional verification, compartmentalization, logging, or supervisory approval requirements.

In some embodiments, the system may determine that a requester is not affiliated with any of the predetermined sectors and may apply a default access policy. In other embodiments, the system may determine that a requester has an unknown or indeterminate affiliation and may request supplemental information, perform enhanced verification, or route the access request to an administrator for review.

The described techniques may be implemented in a centralized access-control platform, a distributed identity-management system, a policy enforcement point, a policy decision point, a zero-trust network architecture, a cloud service, an application gateway, or an application programming interface management system.
